projects.name: Personal website
projects.whatIsThis: A one-page portfolio with a live GitHub contributions heatmap and a résumé that prints from the page itself.
projects.whyThisChoice: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript on GitHub Pages: one page needs no framework or build step, and it deploys on every push.
projects.whatBreaks: The contributions card depends on an outside API and shows 'Loading contributions…' if it fails; the social preview image needs an absolute URL.
projects.whatILearned: DRAFT for Ralston: what building it with a coding agent taught him about reviewing visual changes.

projects.name: Flash Report AI
projects.whatIsThis: A retrieval-augmented app that turns corporate documents (PDF, DOCX, CSV) into cited executive reports, exported as styled DOCX.
projects.whyThisChoice: Retrieval with maximal marginal relevance, so a report draws on several different passages instead of near-duplicates of one.
projects.whatBreaks: Answers are only as good as retrieval: a question whose answer is spread across documents can come back incomplete. It needs an OpenAI key to run.
projects.whatILearned: DRAFT for Ralston: what tuning retrieval taught him about cost and answer quality.

projects.name: Stone Scraper
projects.whatIsThis: Scrapes a web page, cleans the HTML, and lets you ask a local language model to pull structured data out of it.
projects.whyThisChoice: Local models through Ollama, so page content stays on the machine and parsing costs nothing per call.
projects.whatBreaks: Selenium scraping breaks when a site changes its layout or blocks automated browsers; the parse step needs a local Ollama model running.

projects.name: moodle-mcp
projects.whatIsThis: An MCP server (about 950 lines of Python) that lets Claude read a student's Moodle: what's due, course files, announcements and grades.
projects.whyThisChoice: It signs in with the personal token Moodle gives its phone app and calls the app's own web-service API, so it sees exactly what the app sees, without scraping or asking for a password.
projects.whatBreaks: It only works on Moodle sites that allow the mobile app, and stops when the token is revoked or expires.

projects.name: Diagram check (CPSC 415 team project)
projects.role: Team of two with Javier Romo. Ralston built the server, model calls, validator, page and eval (tests first) and wrote the spec; Javier wrote the plan and reviewed.
projects.whatIsThis: A web app that draws a labeled science diagram for a chosen topic, then has a vision model check the picture itself against a hand-written checklist; the grade is computed in code.
projects.whyThisChoice: The critic never sees the generation prompt, so it has to judge the image, and the model never grades itself: our code turns its observations into the verdict.
projects.whatBreaks: The critic misses labels that point at the wrong part: it passed a circuit whose 'wire' label points at the battery.
projects.whatILearned: DRAFT for Ralston: the critic's confident false pass, and why the eval set exists.

projects.name: Receipt reader with an arithmetic check (CPSC 415 lab)
projects.whatIsThis: A command-line tool that reads a receipt photo into JSON with a vision model, then checks in plain code that the items, tax and total add up.
projects.whyThisChoice: The model reads; integer-cent arithmetic decides. Two models were compared on the same receipts before picking the cheaper one.
projects.whatBreaks: Names and dates are not arithmetic, so a misread store name gets through; real photos cost five times the tokens of clean scans.
projects.whatILearned: DRAFT for Ralston: the checker caught a model reading $9.99 as $6.99 while the total was right.
